analysis.title: GS Financials & REITs Sector Specialist: 'Factor Focus' is back?
key_insights: The AI trade is back as it was in the first half of the year. AI vs AI at risk basket (GS Custom Basket) +6% as of send, Datacenters +4% (DC REITs +2-3%), AI Semis +3%.
The move creates a factor setup that favors 12-month high beta momentum and crowded shorts over low-volatility and defensives.
Within financials, large banks (capital markets) and trust banks are outperforming regional banks. Alts are choppy.
Defensives are weak and have leaked lower through the day. Senior Housing REITs are down 4-6%, Exchanges are down (CME is the outlier at -4%), and P&C insurance is weak.
Senior Housing REIT selling is not coming from fundamentals pushback in most conversations. Feedback points to positioning and factors.
P&C insurance bears are vocal and are latching onto negative read-throughs (property reinsurers and RYAN from BRO, workers comp from HIG). The space stabilized after a weak morning.

The crowd is bearish on P&C, but the desk sees no real defense in Senior Housing REITs and Exchanges. Clients are wary of stepping in front of what may be the early stage of a shifting factor backdrop.
FOMC is flagged as a potential big needle mover for the factor backdrop. Factor blaming has been common this year, but today stands out for how quickly feedback went that way.
Most inbounds on tonight's and tomorrow morning's prints are on V, HOOD and LPLA.
PFG is the top print drawing pushback against the move higher, with a question on the earnings call about Samsung in focus.
SPGI bulls are vocal, with many asks about the bear case from here given the ongoing strategic review, in a tough tape for info services.
SOFI is up mid-teens today against crowded short positioning, and clients are asking what is next.

TFC asset sale has mixed feedback but leans positive. A GS note views the deal as accretive to returns (business at 80bps ROA vs 1.1% 3Q26 TFC ROA), and modestly accretive to earnings if paired with securities restructuring.

Other inbounds: BDC M&A read-through to ARES, CBRE trough debate and where the bar is for JLL, CME and CBOE move seen as momentum rather than prediction markets, and Hotels vs Lodging REITs after Feiler said RevPAR was in line while other consumer names point to accelerating revenue trends.
